name: Beef stew with dombolo
summary: Beef stew with steamed bread: tender beef in a rich gravy, with soft yeast dumplings steamed on top in the same pot.
about: Dombolo, also called ujeqe or steamed bread, is a yeast dough cooked by steam rather than baked. In many isiZulu and Sesotho homes it goes on top of a Sunday stew, where it soaks up the flavour from the pot below.

ingredients.name: Beef stock
ingredients.note: made from a cube or powder

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the lukewarm water a little at a time, mixing, until you have a soft dough that is slightly sticky.
Knead on a floured surface for 8 to 10 minutes, until smooth and springy. Put it in an oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.
While the dough rises, heat the oil in a wide heavy pot with a tight lid over medium-high heat. Season the beef and brown it in batches, about 4 minutes a side, until deep brown. Lift out.
Turn the heat to medium. Fry the onions until soft and golden, about 8 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika and fry for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, bay leaves and stock, return the beef, cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the beef is almost tender.
Add the carrots and potatoes, top up with a little water if needed so the stew is just covered, season, and bring back to a steady simmer.
Knock back the dough and shape it into 6 round balls. Set them on top of the stew, a little apart, so they sit on the meat and vegetables rather than sinking.
Cover tightly and steam over low heat for 30 to 35 minutes without lifting the lid. The dombolo is done when it has puffed up and a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Lift the dombolo onto a plate, check the stew is thick and the beef and potatoes are tender, and serve each plate with a dumpling torn open over the gravy.
prepNote: Make the stew a day ahead if you like; reheat to a simmer before steaming fresh dough on top.
